visuals.advice: Add before/after pictures to the description: screenshots for looks, a GIF for motion (drag, animation, open/close, scroll, a multi-step flow). Show the app as production does, never the visual tests' blank fixtures: `npm run gif -- scripts/gif-scenarios/<flow>.ts --dir <PR number>` builds main and this branch for production, reading production's catalog and photos (owner-only screens signed in through the test flags), records the scenario against each with the pointer and keys drawn in, commits the GIFs to the `screenshots` branch under `<PR number>/` and prints the Before/After table to paste. A scenario's play(page, gif) moves with gif.glide, click, drag and scroll, with pauses, never locator.click() or a bare page.mouse (jbhirsh/ci's gif/moves.mjs has the rules), keeps the pointer in frame and ends on a pause; check a few frames, and the long ones, before publishing. Host stills on the `screenshots` branch too, linked at a commit SHA. Or tick "No visible UI change" in the template. Editing the description re-runs this check.

readme-screenshots.source: a local production build reading production's catalog and photos (scripts/readme-screenshots.ts)

visual-baselines.command: npx playwright install --with-deps webkit && npm run test:visual:update

ciFixChecks: `npm run format:check` (`npm run format` rewrites what it flags)
`npm run codegen && git diff --exit-code src/gql/` (if a schema change made `src/gql/` drift, commit the regenerated output too)
the "Bundle size budget" step of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (copy its `run:` commands; after the build)

exempt.PR visuals: Wants pictures in the PR description, which no code change gives (autofix skips its failure too).
